A plain guide to crate labels in detail
A lively round is easier when you know what to expect
Crate Labels for Companion Animal Travel Desk

Proper crate labels support smooth handling from check-in to arrival. At Aurelia Skyways, the Companion Animal Travel Desk reviews each label so the cabin team can identify the animal, confirm the crate belongs to the correct booking, and provide patient attention throughout the journey.

Use a clean label that is firmly attached to the crate in a visible position. Include the traveler name, the animal name if used, and a clear destination reference. Keep the text legible and avoid covering vents, latches, or inspection panels. If a crate has older labels, remove or obscure any outdated information so only the current details remain visible.

The label should also help the desk staff understand handling needs at a glance. Mark the crate in a simple, direct way if the animal needs extra space, quiet placement, or careful loading. Do not attach loose tags that could catch during transfer. If a crate has paperwork pockets, place documents where they can be checked without opening the main compartment.

Before arrival at the skyport, make sure the label is dry, secure, and easy to read. A traveler who prepares the crate in this manner reduces delays at the desk and supports orderly movement through the flight process. If a label is damaged, replace it before presenting the animal for acceptance.

The same attention applies whether the traveler is escorting one pet or several approved animals. Clear labeling helps the team match the right crate with the right itinerary and maintain calm conditions for every animal in care.

For further assistance, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk before travel begins.
